case.paper_title: Human Capital and Development Accounting: New Evidence from Wage Gains at Migration
case.focal_claim: ... immigrants who have never been to high school gain ... more on migration to the United States than immigrants with a college degree (p. 682.)
case.hypothesis: Among immigrants in the authorized wage-gain data, the wage gain from the last home-country job to the last U.S. job is larger for immigrants with no high-school exposure (edyrs <= 8) than for immigrants with a college degree (edyrs >= 16).

tasks_info.task_instruction: In Task 1, the analyst was asked to conduct the analysis without any restrictions.
tasks_info.task_goal: Test whether the focal claim is supported.

tasks_info.task_instruction: You should use the pooled sample of immigrants from poor countries in the NIS (New Immigrant Survey) and the Migration Projects, including Mexico. You should not control for sector: agriculture/nonagriculture, and region i.e. whether an immigrant grew up in a rural or an urban area.
tasks_info.task_goal: Produce one statistical result comparable to the original paper's focal result.

datasets.authorized_only: true. No agent may substitute a dataset not listed here.
datasets.source_type: Survey/archive microdata derived from immigrant wage histories in the New Immigrant Survey and Migration Projects, as represented in the authorized wage-gain table.
datasets.wave_or_subset: Authorized wage_gain_table.xlsx; task instruction identifies it as pooled poor-country immigrants in NIS and Migration Projects including Mexico.
datasets.notes: The authorized Excel file has no source indicator, GDP-per-worker variable, sample weight, rural/urban childhood-region variable, or explicit agriculture/nonagriculture binary. It contains an occupation/sector-like home job group variable, occGroupLastHomeJob, including an Ag category. All inspected columns have 2854 non-null values, but adjusted wage variables have extreme values; log transformation requires positive adjusted wages.

conclusion_rule.statistical_threshold: p < 0.05 describes strong statistical evidence; it does not determine whether a directionally aligned result is support.
conclusion_rule.support_rule: Support when the focal point estimate or pattern is in the expected direction. Opposite requires affirmative evidence of a material effect in the contrary direction; an opposite-signed estimate alone is inconclusive. A non-significant result in the expected direction remains weak directional support.

plan.path_summary: Estimate the focal no-high-school versus college-degree contrast in log wage gains using Tukey biweight robust linear regression. Task1 uses unrestricted controls including available country, demographic, timing, and pre-migration sector/occupation information; Task2 uses the required pooled sample including Mexico and no sector or region controls.

controls: Task1: country, sex, age_home_job, age_home_job_sq, yearLastHomeJob, yearLastUsJob, occGroupLastHomeJob
path_signature.sample_restriction: Authorized wage_gain_table.xlsx rows with positive adjusted home and U.S. wages and nonmissing variables required for each task; Task2 retains Mexico and adds no country/source exclusion.
path_signature.missing_data_rule: Listwise deletion on raw and constructed variables required by each model; drop nonpositive adjusted wages before log transformation.
path_signature.variable_construction: Compute log_wage_gain = log(lastUsWageAdjusted) - log(lastHomeWageAdjusted). Recode edyrs into five groups: no_high_school <=8, some_high_school 9-11, high_school 12, some_college 13-15, college_degree >=16. For Task1 only, compute age_home_job = yearLastHomeJob - yrborn and age_home_job_sq.
path_signature.inference_rule: A positive coefficient for no_high_school relative to college_degree supports the focal claim; p < 0.05 indicates strong statistical evidence and p >= 0.05 with a positive estimate is weak directional support. A negative estimate is inconclusive unless p < 0.05 and the normal-approximation interval excludes zero in the contrary direction.

analysis_path.path_description: Run Tukey biweight robust linear regression of individual log wage gain on paper-aligned education groups, using college degree as the reference and estimating the no-high-school contrast while controlling for available country, sex, age, timing, and pre-migration sector/occupation variables.
preprocessing_steps: Read data/wage_gain_table.xlsx.
Verify that required columns exist: edyrs, lastHomeWageAdjusted, lastUsWageAdjusted, country, sex, yrborn, yearLastHomeJob, yearLastUsJob, occGroupLastHomeJob.
Report starting row count.
Drop rows missing required raw variables and report rows removed.
Drop rows with lastHomeWageAdjusted <= 0 or lastUsWageAdjusted <= 0 and report rows removed.
Compute log_wage_gain as log(lastUsWageAdjusted) - log(lastHomeWageAdjusted).
Recode edyrs into five education groups: no_high_school <= 8; some_high_school 9-11; high_school 12; some_college 13-15; college_degree >= 16.
Compute age_home_job = yearLastHomeJob - yrborn and age_home_job_sq = age_home_job squared.
Drop rows with nonfinite or missing constructed variables and report rows removed.
Estimate robust RLM with TukeyBiweight norm using college_degree as the education reference.

Report the coefficient, normal-approximation standard error, z statistic, p-value, 95% interval, exponentiated proportional difference, final analytic N, and conclusion classification for no_high_school relative to college_degree.

key_choices.main_predictor_measure: Categorical edu_group from edyrs, with no_high_school defined as edyrs <= 8 and college_degree defined as edyrs >= 16.
key_choices.sample_restriction: Authorized dataset rows with positive adjusted wages and nonmissing variables required by the adjusted robust regression.
key_choices.outlier_rule: No rows are trimmed; Tukey biweight robust regression downweights influential residuals.
key_choices.missing_data_rule: Listwise deletion on required raw and constructed variables.
key_choices.data_processing: Log transformation of adjusted wage ratio; education-year categorization; age-at-home-job construction; categorical treatment of education, country, sex, and home occupation/sector group.
key_choices.model_choice: Tukey biweight robust linear regression using statsmodels RLM.
key_choices.inference_rule: An estimate in the expected positive direction is support; p < 0.05 is strong statistical evidence and p >= 0.05 is weak directional support. A negative estimate is opposite only with affirmative evidence of a material contrary effect; otherwise it is inconclusive.

models.formula: log_wage_gain ~ C(edu_group, Treatment(reference="college_degree")) + C(country) + C(sex) + age_home_job + age_home_job_sq + yearLastHomeJob + yearLastUsJob + C(occGroupLastHomeJob)
models.planned_estimation: Robust-regression coefficient for no_high_school relative to college_degree in log_wage_gain, plus exponentiated proportional difference exp(coef)-1.
models.inference_criteria: Support if the coefficient is positive; p < 0.05 indicates strong evidence and p >= 0.05 indicates weak directional support. A negative coefficient is opposite only if p < 0.05, otherwise inconclusive.
models.qualification: The focal outcome and contrast are preserved. Tukey biweight robust regression is a defensible robustness analysis because inspected adjusted wage variables contain extreme values, and it differs from prior OLS, median quantile, trimmed OLS, and Huber paths without choosing a method based on expected results. Task1 is unrestricted, and the available sector/occupation variable is paper-relevant because the paper summary notes prior employment sector as a determinant of wage gains.

outcome.missing_data_handling: Drop rows with missing or nonpositive adjusted wages or nonfinite constructed log_wage_gain.

method_justification.claim_alignment: Both tasks estimate the no-high-school versus college-degree difference in wage gains from migration to the United States, the operational form of the focal claim.
method_justification.dataset_alignment: Both tasks use only the authorized original data/wage_gain_table.xlsx file. Task2 treats this file as the required pooled poor-country NIS/Migration Projects sample and retains Mexico.
method_justification.method_reason: Log wage gain is directly constructible from adjusted home and U.S. wages and matches the paper's wage-gain framing.
